hypotheses.claim: Under otherwise matched P01 conditions, substituting TEA for TEOA changes the CO/H2 distribution; if the difference disappears after strict matching and full controls, the original observation was condition-dependent rather than additive-specific. A discriminating prediction is that CO and H2 both change in a reproducible donor-dependent direction only when catalyst, ligand, absorber, medium, gas handling, and analysis are held fixed.
hypotheses.alternative: Apparent TEA/TEOA differences mainly reflect uncontrolled changes in medium composition, background photochemistry, donor consumption, or assay conditions rather than a real donor-identity effect on the Co-bpy catalytic manifold.
hypotheses.platform_and_comparator_choice: Primary test in P01 because it preserves the CoCl2+bpy, g-C3N4, MeCN/H2O, TEOA baseline closest to the researcher context; TEA is the single-variable comparator. P02 is supplementary only to check whether any donor trend survives in a cleaner homogeneous cobalt assay.
hypotheses.uncertainty: No supplied source gives a strict within-paper TEA-versus-TEOA head-to-head in the exact P01 recipe, so reproducibility and comparability must be confirmed before inferring mechanism. Background CO/H2 formation without catalyst is documented in related systems, which could compress or distort observed selectivity shifts.

candidates.title: Matched TEA/TEOA benchmark
candidates.purpose: Test whether changing the amine from TEOA to TEA alone alters CO/H2 distribution in the P01 Co-bpy/g-C3N4 platform under intentionally unmatched conditions to maximize donor contrast.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV059 and GX012 motivate a cobalt-containing photocatalytic CO2-reduction comparison using TEOA and TEA. EV063 suggests medium can matter, so the proposal transfers this by changing donor identity while also allowing donor-driven medium differences to remain, treating any resulting product shift as additive-specific. EV081, EV045, and EV022 support measuring CO and H2 together and including simple catalytic context controls.

procedure: Assemble the P01 TEOA formulation from the supplied system description and prepare TEA and no-amine variants by copying the same nominal setup.
Run illuminated CO2 photocatalysis for all groups in parallel reactors without additional matching adjustments so the donor environments remain naturally distinct.
Analyze headspace by the same GC workflow for CO and H2, preferably at one endpoint and one interim sample.
Compare product amounts and CO/H2 ratios across groups and rank donor effects by absolute difference.
measurements: GC-detected CO amount
GC-detected H2 amount
CO/H2 ratio or selectivity descriptor
Qualitative note of visible instability or precipitation after reaction
candidates.supports: A reproducible difference between E01G01 and E01G02 in either CO/H2 ratio or both product amounts supports H01 and is interpreted as mainly caused by amine identity.
candidates.refutes: Near-identical CO and H2 outcomes for E01G01 and E01G02 refute a meaningful donor effect in this platform.
candidates.inconclusive: Large run-to-run scatter, strong signals in E01G03, or obvious formulation instability make the comparison inconclusive.
candidates.parameter_selection: Use the literature-grounded P01 TEOA formulation as the starting benchmark. If exact numeric settings are missing, select them by a short pilot that maximizes total gas production in the TEOA case, then copy the same nominal settings to TEA and no-amine without further correction.
candidates.limitations: This design wrongly treats donor substitution as a single-variable test even though amine identity can alter medium composition, proton behavior, and CO2 interactions. It does not isolate mechanism and weakly controls background artifacts.

candidates.title: Matched donor-specific necessity and background controls
candidates.purpose: Test whether any TEA versus TEOA CO/H2 difference persists only in the complete photocatalytic formulation after symmetric light, gas-feed, and cobalt-necessity controls for both donors.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV046, EV081, EV045, and GX008 support negative controls for light, CO2 versus inert gas, and key component omission, while EV081 and GX012 show that catalyst-free or altered-component backgrounds can still produce some gas. The proposal narrows transfer to assay-validation logic in the P01 donor comparison and does not assume these controls alone identify mechanism.

procedure: Prepare one matched reaction matrix for both donors, changing only amine identity within each donor pair and holding reactor format, nominal loadings, solvent composition, gas handling, and GC method constant.
Run full, dark, inert-gas, and no-cobalt groups for both donors in the same campaign with randomized position/order if possible.
Quantify CO and H2 for every group by the same calibrated GC workflow and compare each control only to its donor-matched full system before comparing donors.
Interpret donor effects only after symmetric controls show that full-system signals exceed donor-matched backgrounds by a practically meaningful margin under the same assay window.

candidates.supports: H01 is supported if TEA and TEOA full systems reproducibly differ in CO and/or H2 distribution while both donors show low dark, inert-gas, and no-cobalt outputs relative to their own full systems.
candidates.refutes: H01 is weakened or refuted for this platform if the TEA and TEOA full systems converge within experimental uncertainty after strict matching, or if one or both donors show control outputs comparable to the corresponding full system so that the apparent donor effect is explained by backgrounds.
candidates.inconclusive: The result is inconclusive if full-system signals are near detection limits, if donor-specific controls are non-negligible and differ between donors, or if instability prevents fair comparison across the reaction window.
candidates.parameter_selection: Use the same nominal baseline formulation for all eight groups. If all groups are near detection limits, extend irradiation time equally for the entire matrix in a pilot until at least one full system is quantifiable above blank noise. Do not optimize TEA and TEOA separately inside this control card; keep any later donor-specific optimization outside the matched assay-validation test.
candidates.limitations: This card tests assay validity and donor dependence under one matched formulation but does not isolate why donors differ. No-cobalt omission does not separately test ligand or absorber necessity. Equal nominal conditions do not guarantee equal pH, donor consumption, or active-species population, so mechanistic interpretation remains bounded.

EV063 indicates medium composition affects CO/H2 in a CoCl2/bpy-related system. EV059 motivates applying such amount variation within the P01 TEOA/TEA comparison and interpreting the combined landscape as donor behavior.

procedure: Choose two donor loadings spanning a visible performance range by brief pilot in the TEOA system, then reuse the same nominal low and high levels for TEA.
Run the four illuminated CO2 photocatalysis groups with all other nominal settings unchanged.
Measure CO and H2 by the same GC workflow and compare both within-donor amount trends and cross-donor differences at each amount.
Use the resulting pattern to decide whether donor identity or donor amount is the stronger determinant.

candidates.supports: If TEA and TEOA remain separated at both low and high donor amounts, H01 is supported and the donor effect is treated as intrinsic rather than condition-dependent.
candidates.refutes: If changing donor amount dominates while TEA and TEOA overlap at one or both levels, H01 is refuted.
candidates.inconclusive: Crossing trends, strong instability, or poor signal at one loading make the identity conclusion inconclusive.
candidates.parameter_selection: Define low and high donor amounts by a short pilot that finds one underperforming and one stronger TEOA condition. Apply the same nominal low and high amounts to TEA without compensating for compositional differences, because identical nominal addition is assumed to create the fairest comparison.
candidates.limitations: This combines donor identity and medium perturbation issues and overinterprets nominally matched additions as chemically matched conditions. Two-point amount sampling can miss nonmonotonic behavior and cannot isolate mechanism.

candidates.title: TEA versus TEOA donor-side quenching comparison in the verified P01 baseline matrix
candidates.purpose: Test whether replacing TEOA with TEA changes upstream photoredox observables in a verified P01 baseline formulation under strictly matched nonreactive measurement conditions, as a descriptive covariate for any donor-dependent CO/H2 shift without claiming catalytic causation.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV053 and EV065 support transferable fluorescence/UV-vis quenching logic in donor-containing cobalt photocatalytic systems; GX007 indicates TEA-for-TEOA substitution can alter photochemical behavior; EV011 supports that TEA and TEOA form different donor-derived radical intermediates after quenching. Proposed transfer: use the verified P01 catalytic formulation as the starting matrix, then adapt it only as needed for optical measurement with matched cobalt-containing and cobalt-free references to separate donor-side from cobalt-associated effects. This is proposed characterization, not proof that the same observable controls catalysis.

procedure: First verify the actual P01 baseline composition and prepare matched optical samples that differ only in donor identity or cobalt-component presence across groups.

Record absorber-centered fluorescence and/or UV-vis spectra under identical cuvette geometry, excitation settings, and background subtraction rules, including solvent-only and absorber-free backgrounds when needed.

Use a pilot to adjust optical density into the instrument-linear range and to check whether scattering, adsorption, or donor addition causes unacceptable inner-filter distortion; if so, restrict interpretation to corrected descriptive comparisons or dilute all groups equally.

Compare TEA and TEOA trends first in cobalt-free samples and then in cobalt-containing samples, retaining raw spectra and using Stern-Volmer-style summaries only where empirical linearity is demonstrated.
measurements: Steady-state fluorescence intensity of the absorber-containing sample under matched excitation
Optional fluorescence lifetime proxy only if available and if scattering permits meaningful extraction
UV-vis absorbance or difference spectra before and after donor addition or short irradiation exposure
Background absorbance and scattering from donor, solvent matrix, and cobalt-containing mixtures
Empirical quenching trend summaries for cobalt-free and cobalt-containing matrices
candidates.supports: A reproducible TEA-versus-TEOA difference in optical quenching or spectral response under otherwise matched conditions, especially if the donor ordering is observed in repeated preparations and survives background correction, supports H01 only in the narrowed sense that donor identity changes upstream photoredox behavior in the verified matrix. If the difference appears only when cobalt components are present, that further supports involvement of cobalt-associated interactions but still does not establish the catalytic mechanism.
candidates.refutes: If TEA and TEOA show no reproducible difference within calibrated detection limits in both cobalt-free and cobalt-containing matched matrices, a large donor-specific upstream optical difference is disfavored as the main explanation for any CO/H2 shift, while leaving downstream proton management, catalyst speciation, and assay artifacts unresolved.
candidates.inconclusive: Results are inconclusive if scattering, adsorption, unstable baselines, donor-dependent decomposition, or noncomparable optical densities prevent reliable matched comparison. A measured optical difference is also inconclusive for catalytic causation unless linked separately to catalytic data.
candidates.parameter_selection: Use the verified P01 baseline identities and nominal component levels as the starting point. Any dilution or path-length adjustment needed for optical work must be applied equally across all groups and documented as an adaptation from the catalytic matrix. Pilot criteria: keep absorbance in an empirically linear instrumental range, avoid complete signal extinction, and accept Stern-Volmer analysis only over the observed linear region; otherwise report matched-point descriptive differences only.
candidates.limitations: This is characterization, not a catalytic readout. In a g-C3N4-containing or otherwise scattering matrix, fluorescence and UV-vis assignments can be compromised by adsorption, inner-filter effects, and turbidity. Even with cobalt-free controls, the experiment cannot identify the turnover-relevant intermediate or prove that a donor-dependent optical change causes a donor-dependent CO/H2 shift. Transfer from EV053, EV065, GX007, and EV011 is methodological and donor-chemistry based, not direct proof for the exact P01 catalytic manifold.

candidates.title: Near-operando cobalt-state comparison under TEOA and TEA
candidates.purpose: Assess whether TEA and TEOA correlate with different cobalt-associated oxidation or coordination signatures in the P01-like system under matched conditions, while keeping inference descriptive unless donor-linked differences survive donor-matched backgrounds and matched timing.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV059 anchors the closest supplied formulation family: CoCl2 plus bpy with g-C3N4 in MeCN/H2O using TEOA, with triethylamine noted among related donor variants. GX008 supports operando-capable spectroscopy and strict controls for photocatalytic CO2 reduction. EV046 supports catalyst-free/background references and warns that before/after or recovered-state characterization alone cannot identify the operating catalyst. Proposed transfer: compare TEA and TEOA only within a matched P01-like matrix, add donor-matched cobalt-free references for both donors, and interpret donor effects as correlation with cobalt-state signatures rather than proof of mechanism.

procedure: Choose one cobalt-sensitive spectroscopic readout available for the actual sample state and add one independent cross-check if feasible.

Acquire donor-matched cobalt-containing and cobalt-free reference data before illumination, then repeat at a fixed illuminated-state sampling point using identical handling and timing for both donors.
Use a pilot to set concentration, path length, acquisition time, and illumination window so cobalt-associated signal is measurable without saturating the detector or fully degrading the sample.
Interpret only reproducible donor-dependent features that remain after donor-matched background subtraction or comparison and, if possible, agree with the second readout.

candidates.supports: A reproducible TEA-versus-TEOA difference in cobalt-associated signatures under matched illuminated conditions, especially when smaller or absent before illumination and absent in donor-matched cobalt-free backgrounds, supports a donor-linked change in the cobalt-containing manifold.
candidates.refutes: If TEA and TEOA show no reproducible difference in cobalt-associated signatures before or at the matched illuminated state within method resolution, a large donor-specific cobalt-state difference is disfavored as the main explanation for CO/H2 changes.
candidates.inconclusive: Signals dominated by support or donor background, assignments visible equally in cobalt-free references, or differences seen only in recovered samples are inconclusive. Even a clear donor-dependent cobalt signature does not alone prove the active species or the cause of product selectivity.
candidates.parameter_selection: No exact spectroscopic settings are supplied. Use pilot scans to determine a measurable cobalt signal range, unsaturated acquisition settings, and the shortest illumination interval that produces a detectable state change without complete decomposition. Hold reactor geometry, gas handling, optical flux, and quench timing constant across donor conditions.
candidates.limitations: Assignments in a mixed support-plus-molecular matrix remain uncertain, and before-versus-illuminated comparisons are time-coupled rather than isolated causal tests. This card addresses state correlation under matched donors, not full active-species identification or causal pathway separation.

candidates.title: 13CO2 origin check for CO under matched TEOA and TEA conditions

EV046, EV022, EV082, and GX008 support transferable use of 13CO2, GC-MS, and negative controls in photocatalytic CO2-reduction studies. Proposed transfer: apply donor-matched 13CO2 labeling and donor-matched catalyst-omission negatives to the same P01-like benchmark workflow, and interpret carbon origin separately from donor-effect or mechanism claims.

measurements: GC-MS isotopic pattern for CO under 13CO2 and under unlabeled CO2 references
CO and H2 amounts from the same matched runs to preserve donor-comparison context

candidates.supports: Detection of the expected labeled CO signature in both donor conditions, with corresponding unlabeled reference patterns in natural-abundance runs and little or no labeled CO in the donor-matched catalyst-omission controls, supports the claim that observed CO in the TEA/TEOA comparison is genuinely CO2-derived under both donors.
candidates.refutes: If a donor condition shows CO without the expected labeled signature under 13CO2, or if comparable labeled CO appears in the matched catalyst-omission control for that donor, the CO comparison is undermined by artifact or background formation concerns.
candidates.inconclusive: Very low CO signal, overlapping fragments, carryover, or inconsistent gas handling can leave origin assignment inconclusive. Even a positive 13CO2 result does not identify why TEA and TEOA differ; it only addresses carbon origin and catalyst dependence of detected CO.
candidates.parameter_selection: Use the same matched formulation, reactor, illumination program, and sampling schedule as the verified benchmark. Because no isotope-analysis recipe is supplied, first establish GC-MS discrimination between labeled and unlabeled CO with instrument-specific checks, then choose sampling volume and run time to detect the smallest benchmark CO signal without overload. If signal remains marginal, prioritize the donor-matched labeled pairs and donor-matched catalyst-omission negatives over expanding the matrix.
candidates.limitations: This card verifies product origin and bounds catalyst dependence of labeled CO detection; it does not resolve whether donor effects arise from photophysics, proton management, medium composition, or cobalt-state changes. Before/after agreement in product origin cannot by itself establish the operating-state mechanism.

evidence.claim: Literature reports a g-C3N4-assisted molecular CO2 photoreduction formulation using CoCl2 plus bipyridine to form Co(bpy)3Cl2 in MeCN/H2O with TEOA, and the table explicitly lists alternative amines including triethylamine with different CO/H2 selectivities under related conditions.
evidence.transfer_limit: The exact active cobalt species may depend on in situ assembly and support effects from g-C3N4 or Co-ZIF-9; the snippet does not provide a direct TEA-versus-TEOA head-to-head in one unchanged formulation, so transfer to the researcher's specific Co(II)-bipyridine system requires verification.
evidence.reason: This is the closest direct match to the target topic because it explicitly combines cobalt chloride and bipyridine in a CO2 photocatalytic system and mentions TEOA while tabulating triethylamine and other amines as donor variants affecting CO/H2 selectivity. It supports selecting this formulation family for controlled TEA/TEOA comparison, while preserving uncertainty about species identity and exact comparability.

evidence.transfer_limit: Relevant because it uses a cobalt photocatalyst and TEOA in homogeneous CO2 reduction, but the catalyst is 1-Co rather than an explicitly verified Co(II)-bipyridine complex, the photosensitizer is Ru(phen)3 rather than the user's unspecified absorber, and no TEA comparator appears in the snippet.
evidence.reason: This snippet directly supports a plausible primary comparison platform anchored in a cobalt molecular photocatalytic system with TEOA and measurable CO evolution. It also contributes a transferable mechanistic observable via quenching analysis. Its value is limited by incomplete catalyst identity within the snippet and lack of TEA comparison.

evidence.reason: Useful for generating competing explanations for donor-dependent product distributions: donor effects may arise from reductive quenching kinetics, proton-transfer behavior, or CO2 capture/solvation chemistry rather than intrinsic cobalt-site changes. It is transferable as hypothesis support with explicit system and interpretation limits.

evidence.transfer_limit: This supports medium-composition comparators in a Co(II)-bipyridine-containing photocatalytic system, but the photosensitizer/semiconductor platform and ionic-liquid component differ from the researcher's unspecified baseline. It informs controllable formulation variables more than the specific TEA/TEOA cause.
evidence.reason: Relevant because it explicitly uses CoCl2 and bipyridine in photocatalytic CO2 reduction with CO/H2 as outputs and demonstrates that product distribution is sensitive to medium composition. This strengthens the need for strict comparability controls when testing TEA versus TEOA in related systems.

major_issues: The stated purpose and inference explicitly rely on intentionally unmatched donor environments, so any TEA/TEOA difference is confounded by medium composition, proton behavior, CO2 interactions, and other donor-driven formulation changes rather than isolated donor identity.

The card claims the TEA-versus-TEOA contrast is a single-variable test because nominal settings are copied, but the supplied evidence warns that equal nominal addition does not chemically match the systems and that medium strongly affects CO/H2 output.

The proposed interpretation overstates causality by treating any observed product shift as additive-specific even though strong catalyst-free or donor/background contributions are already documented in related systems.
decisions.rationale: EV059 gives the closest direct platform family and indicates TEOA-containing Co/bpy/g-C3N4 CO2 photoreduction with mention of alternative amines, but not a strict head-to-head under unchanged conditions. EV063 directly cautions that medium ratio can strongly alter CO/H2 in a CoCl2/bpy-related photocatalytic system. EV081 and EV022 show that background pathways and donor effects can change apparent outputs without proving donor-specific catalytic control. Because this card intentionally preserves donor-induced medium differences and then interprets any difference as direct evidence for donor identity, the proposed inference is not valid for H01 as stated. It could generate exploratory observations, but the card's own support/refute logic is too strong and misleading.

major_issues: The control set is asymmetric across donors: dark is only run for TEOA, Ar only for TEA, and no-cobalt only for TEOA, so donor-specific background artifacts are not equivalently bounded for the TEA/TEOA comparison.

The card concludes that limited controls are sufficient to interpret the TEA/TEOA difference as intrinsic, but the supplied evidence only supports control logic in general, not sufficiency of this compact and unbalanced set.
Some key contrasts are multi-factor or nonparallel when used to validate the donor comparison, weakening inference about whether backgrounds differ by donor identity.
decisions.rationale: This is a useful candidate because EV046, EV081, EV045, and GX008 directly support negative controls, assay validation, and origin/background checking in photocatalytic CO2-reduction workflows. The card also keeps the main full-system TEA/TEOA comparison in view. However, the proposed compact control set does not actually test donor-specific backgrounds symmetrically, so it cannot justify the claim that remaining TEA/TEOA differences are intrinsic. A revised version with matched dark, inert-gas/no-CO2, and key omission controls for both donors would be defensible and valuable as assay-validation support for H01.

major_issues: Low and high donor amounts are selected by optimizing only the TEOA case and then copied to TEA, so the cross-donor comparisons are not chemically matched and are biased by donor-specific medium/basicity/CO2-solvation differences.
The card explicitly merges donor identity and donor amount into one causal factor, which does not answer the stated hypothesis about donor identity under otherwise matched conditions.

The proposed refutation logic is invalid: overlap at one or both loadings does not refute a donor-identity effect because amount-dependent nonlinearity and confounding can mask or reshape differences.
Two-point amount sampling is too limited for the strong causal interpretation claimed, especially when medium effects are already known to alter CO/H2 distributions.
decisions.rationale: EV061 and EV063 support the idea that donor concentration and medium composition can strongly affect photocatalytic outputs, but that is exactly why this design cannot isolate donor identity. EV059 motivates working within the P01 family, yet the card's comparison logic overinterprets nominally matched additions as fair identity tests. As written, it may be an exploratory response-surface screen, but it is not valid evidence for or against H01's donor-identity claim and its stated support/refute criteria are unsound.

major_issues: The proposal is only indirectly linked to H01 because quenching or spectral differences are upstream covariates, not catalytic proof of the cause of CO/H2 changes.

In a heterogeneous g-C3N4-containing matrix, scattering, adsorption, and inner-filter effects may compromise fluorescence/UV-vis assignment unless background subtraction and descriptive limits are enforced.

The card refers to a P01-like matched formulation rather than the verified catalytic benchmark itself, so exact transfer of observed photophysical differences to the catalytic manifold remains uncertain.
decisions.rationale: This is a constructive characterization candidate. EV053 and EV065 support transferable quenching/UV-vis logic in donor-containing cobalt photocatalytic contexts, GX007 directly indicates TEA-for-TEOA substitution can alter photochemical behavior, and EV011 supports donor-specific radical/reactivity differences. The card appropriately includes cobalt-free and cobalt-containing matched references and already limits interpretation to a covariate rather than full mechanism. Because the main risks are signal assignment and transfer limits rather than fatal design flaws, this should be revised for strict optical controls and descriptive interpretation, not rejected.

major_issues: Cobalt-state assignment in the mixed heterogeneous/solution P01-like matrix is uncertain, and overlapping donor/support/background features can make oxidation or coordination claims ambiguous unless the readout is carefully bounded.
The before-versus-illuminated comparisons are inherently time-coupled and descriptive, so they cannot by themselves establish causal donor effects on the active catalytic state.

The background reference is underspecified because E05G05 allows 'TEOA or TEA matched separately in pilot', which weakens direct donor-specific background assignment unless both donor-matched cobalt-free references are included.
decisions.rationale: This candidate has good value as a near-operando characterization option rather than a decisive mechanism test. EV059 anchors the relevant formulation family, while GX008 and EV046 support operando-capable spectroscopy, background references, and caution against overinterpreting recovered-state data. The card largely respects those limits and aims to compare matched pre- and illuminated states under each donor. It should be revised to require donor-matched cobalt-free references and to keep conclusions descriptive and correlation-based. Given those constraints, it is worth retaining despite specialist resources.

major_issues: The labeled negative control is not fully matched because only one donor identity may be used there, so donor-specific background labeled CO formation cannot be equivalently excluded for both TEA and TEOA.
This card can verify carbon origin but not the cause of TEA/TEOA selectivity differences, so any interpretation must stay separated from mechanistic claims about donor identity.
GC-MS assignment at low signal is vulnerable to memory effects and fragment overlap, so instrument validation is necessary before using small differences in labeled CO as inference support.
decisions.rationale: This is a strong supportive candidate for assay validation. EV021 directly shows that TEOA can be non-innocent yet isotope labeling can still confirm CO2 as the source of CO. EV046, EV082, EV022, and GX008 support transferable use of 13CO2, GC-MS, and negative controls in photocatalytic CO2-reduction studies. The card correctly frames origin verification separately from selectivity and mechanism, which is appropriate. It needs revision only to make donor-matched negative controls explicit and to maintain bounded interpretation.

previous_review.overall: Across the six candidates, none merits shortlist because each retains substantive inferential or control limitations. E01 and E03 should be rejected because they explicitly overclaim donor-identity causality from chemically unmatched or conflated comparisons. E02, E04, E05, and E06 are worth retaining in revised form: E02 as a more symmetric necessity/background control set, E04 as a bounded photophysical covariate study, E05 as descriptive near-operando cobalt-state characterization, and E06 as an origin check that protects against carbon-source artifacts. The supplied evidence most directly supports the need for strict matching, balanced controls, descriptive characterization, and isotopic verification rather than strong mechanistic conclusions from nominally matched donor substitutions alone.
